sweep_summary: Slavomolisano (slav1254) is in the catalog as 'tonal' on Breu & Piccoli 2000 (grammar part of the Acquaviva dictionary). The title search produced exactly one item, Vitale, Boula de Mareüil & De Meo 2017 on Chinese L2 Italian polar questions, which Glottolog's own reference page says was attached to svm by a computerized assignment on the word 'sviluppo' — not relevant, priority none. Crossref returned nothing new on Molise Slavic accent) and Breu's Konstanz 'acqua' site. From that site I downloaded the catalog's deciding source itself, 38 pp..), with; the catalog quotation is verbatim at p. 388, and p. 389 adds that the two tones are distinctive only on the first/only syllable (minimal pairs nos/nos, bila/bila, kupit/kupit) and that length is contrastive only under the falling tone. Rešetar 1911 §§72-74 (held by the project from the compilation of 9/16) independently confirms a new-Štokavian accent position with frequent double accentuation. Coding 'tonal' stands; no source read contradicts it. Still unread and print-only (from the existing list of works to obtain, not from this search of works with stress in the title's items): Barone 1995 phonology of Acquaviva (high), Breu 1999 'Phonologie und Verbkonjugation im Moliseslavischen' (medium), Sammartino 2004 grammar of Montemitro (medium).

new_statements.translation: It is above all a double accentuation of two successive syllables of equal force or with more force on the second syllable, though often in fact accompanied by a rise in fundamental frequency (f0). [...] The tones are distinctive only on the first or – unlike in Croatian – on the only syllable of the word. As minimal pairs we cite e.g. nos 'nose' : nos 'carry! (imper. sg. of nosit)' or bila 'been (ppp of bit)' : bila 'white' for long vowels, and kupit 'to gather' : kupit 'to buy' for short ones.
new_statements.citation: Breu, Walter & Piccoli, Giovanni (con la collaborazione di Snježana Marčec) 2000. Dizionario croato molisano di Acquaviva Collecroce. Campobasso. Parte grammaticale, author's e-format 2011 ('© 2011 Walter Breu (Costanza, Germania)'), sec. 1.2 'Fonologia soprasegmentale (quantità, accento e toni)', pp. 388-389.
new_statements.reading: First-hand description of the Acquaviva Collecroce variety by the leading specialist. Two word-tones ('discendente' = ordinary single stress as in Italian; 'ascendente' = a double accentuation over two successive syllables, or over the two moras of one long syllable, usually with an f0 rise). The tones are lexically contrastive and are contrastive only on the first (or only) syllable of the word (minimal pairs given); vowel length is contrastive only under the falling tone. Position of the falling accent is not given by a rule in this section; the rising accent is inherited from the Štokavian retraction and is productive in loans. This is the same passage the catalog quotes (catalog_quote found verbatim at p. 388), so it confirms the current 'tonal' coding rather than superseding it. Rešetar 1911 (Ital. transl., e-ed. 2001, §§72-74, pp. 107-109, already held by the project as RES-3) adds the position statement that the dialect follows the new-Štokavian principle as to accent POSITION ('va decisamente definita come basantesi – per quanto riguarda la posizione dell'accento – sul principio dell'accentazione štocava nuova', §73 p. 108) with frequent double accentuation (stronger on the original syllable, higher/rising on the preceding one) — the historical antecedent of Breu's 'tono ascendente'.

tone_statements.quote: #ˈv, #ˈvː fallender Ton auf Kurz- oder Langvokal auf der 1. oder einzigen Silbe ... v́.vː, v́.v steigender Ton auf Kurzvokal vor Lang- oder Kurzvokal (Doppelakzent), etwa balūn [báluːn] ‘Wildbach’, kupit [kúpit] ‘kaufen’ v́ː.v̥, v́ː# steigender Ton auf einem Langvokal nur vor Flüstervokal oder in der letzten (oder einzigen) Silbe eines Wortes ... Der Fallton im Wortinnern prosodisch nicht vollständig integrierter Lehnwörter und der Steigton auf einer letzten oder einzigen Silbe unterscheidet das Tonalsystem des MSL in grundlegender Weise vom System der BKS-Standardsprachen.
tone_statements.translation: #ˈv, #ˈvː falling tone on a short or long vowel on the 1st or only syllable ... v́.vː, v́.v rising tone on a short vowel before a long or short vowel (double accent), e.g. balūn [báluːn] 'torrent', kupit [kúpit] 'to buy'; v́ː.v̥, v́ː# rising tone on a long vowel only before a whispered vowel or in the last (or only) syllable of a word ... The falling tone word-internally in prosodically not fully integrated loanwords and the rising tone on a last or only syllable distinguish the tonal system of Molise Slavic fundamentally from the system of the BCS standard languages.
tone_statements.locator: p. 21 (schema of suprasegmental combinations), Einleitung §3 'Phonetik und Phonologie' pp. 17-21; also pp. 12-13 §2 notation ('tonal und dynamisch: Doppelakzentuierung des Moliseslavischen') and p. 19 (length-tone interaction), p. 20 (final/monosyllabic rising tone, Doppelakzent)

tone_statements.quote: Akcentuacija govora moliških Hrvata očuvala je i do danas temeljne izvorne osobine. Svi silabemi mogu biti dugi i kratki, naglašeni i nenaglašeni. U dugih se naglašenih silabema javlja i intonacijska razlikovnost (uzlaznost ~ silaznost). Kod kratkih silabema intonacijska opreka nije sustavno utvrđena, iako se mogu registrirati ostvaraji uzlazno ili silazno intonirani. ... Iz izloženoga izlazi da se u moliškom hrvatskom mogu pojaviti ove akcenatsko-kvantitativne kvalitete: ... (tj. dugi uzlazni akcent zvan akut, dugi silazni akcent zvan dugosilazni, kratki akcent, duga nenaglašena kvantiteta zvana dužina, kratka nenaglašena kvantiteta zvana kračina).
tone_statements.translation: The accentuation of the speech of the Molise Croats has preserved its basic original features to this day. All syllabics can be long and short, stressed and unstressed. In long stressed syllabics an intonational (tonal) distinction also appears (rising ~ falling). In short syllabics the intonational opposition is not systematically established, although rising- or falling-intoned realisations can be registered. ... From the above it follows that the following accentual-quantitative qualities can occur in Molise Croatian: ... (i.e. a long rising accent called acute, a long falling accent, a short accent, long unstressed quantity called length, short unstressed quantity called shortness).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 127-128, section on phonology/accentuation of the three village dialects
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: 3 accents: long rising, long falling, short (no tone contrast on shorts) + unstressed length; frequent double/triple accent; heavy variation.

sources.note: Citation + second-hand summaries: the standard OLA 'fonološki opis' format includes the prosodic system (accent, tone, quantity, distribution). Sujoldžić et al. 1987 p. 127 report that Brozović - unlike Rešetar - disregarded the rising/falling opposition on short stressed vowels (one short accent only, tonal contrast on longs) and gave 'a more realistic picture' than Rešetar 1911; Breu 2017 fn. 12 says Brozović (1981) 'hatte noch keinerlei Klarheit gebracht' on the prosodic processes.

tone.summary: Reportedly: tone contrast on long stressed syllables only, single short accent (second-hand).
